newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian city cracks down on killer bikers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian city cracks down on killer bikers.

text.p: The port city of Barranquilla has banned motorcyclists from carrying passengers aged over 14 to stem a wave of contract killings every year near Christmas.
The ban begins on Nov. 1 and lasts until after Christmas, covering the Caribbean city's "slaying season" when the murder rate soars, policeman Carlos Rodriguez said.
"This ban is a preventive measure to cut the murder rate over Christmas and, if successful, we could reintroduce it at Carnival time in February," he said.

Gunning down victims from a motorcycle and then making a fast getaway through traffic is a favourite method of hired assassins in Colombia, which has one of the world's highest murder rates -- 80 homicides for every 100,000 inhabitants, according to Pan-American Health Organisation figures.
Two men died and five were wounded in Barranquilla last month when drive-by assassins open fire on a group playing dominoes.
